content:
Sam (Finance): FYI Vera on our SOC account reported two invoices for the same month after their mid-cycle upgrade. Looks like platform fee proration duplicated across INV-2026-0789 and INV-2026-0790. Total overcharge ~ $1,125.

Priya (RevOps): Can you paste the invoice lines? Need to see dates/periods and PO.

Sam (Finance): Pasting extracted lines from PDFs:
```
INV-2026-0789 (issued 2026-02-01)
  - private-standard | platform-fee (prorated 02/01 - 02/14) | $1,125.00
INV-2026-0790 (issued 2026-02-15)
  - private-prem     | platform-fee (prorated 02/15 - 03/01) | $1,125.00
```
Customer says they'd expect only the delta charge once, not two full prorated platform fee lines. PO: PO-1122, Contract SOW-ACCT-2025.

Marta (Billing): Our proration job creates an invoice for each activation/deactivation event. In this case the upgrade window closed at 00:00 UTC and the catalog still had the old SKU tag for a few minutes; system treated them as separate prorated charges. OpsBot scheduled job log shows two invoice jobs ran.

OpsBot: Job billing-prorate-run-2026-02-15 completed. Generated invoice ids [INV-2026-0789, INV-2026-0790]. Note: invoice split due to two active sku_tags during transition window.

Darren (Sales): Customer explicitly told our AE they upgraded effective 02/15 local time. They are upset about duplicate platform-fee lines. They want a corrected invoice and refund for the overlapping prorated amount.

Priya (RevOps): Is the overlap amount exactly one of the prorated lines ($1,125)? Or should we compute delta (new minus old)?

Sam (Finance): They were charged two separate prorates that collectively equal one month's platform fee. Customer expectation: single prorated difference (i.e., charge only for remaining period at new SKU minus credit for the remainder of old SKU). In practice that would net to $0 extra beyond the proper delta. Given complexity and small amount, propose issuing a credit of $1,125 to cancel the duplicate prorated charge (effectively refunding the earlier prorate).

Marta (Billing): We can issue a credit note and apply it to INV-2026-0789. Because INV-2026-0789 is already paid, refund to card will be processed. Need approval from RevOps + Sales to proceed.

Darren (Sales): Approved. Please include a short customer note explaining "proration overlap during SKU transition" and steps we've taken. CC me and CS.

Priya (RevOps): Approved as well. Please reference internal ticket BILL-9019 for the engineering fix.

Marta (Billing): Creating credit note CN-2026-0025 for $1,125.00 against INV-2026-0789. ETA refund 24-48h. Adding memo: "proration overlap during SKU transition, customer-initiated upgrade 02/15 local time".

Sam (Finance): Thanks. @Darren can you notify the customer and set expectation on timing? Also please confirm whether we should adjust March invoice to avoid any residual rounding.

Darren (Sales): Sent a short note to customer: "We're issuing CN-2026-0025 to refund the duplicate prorated platform fee. Refund will hit your card in 1-2 business days. We've logged an internal fix to prevent recurrence." Customer replied with ":+1: thanks".

Marta (Billing): Credit created and refund queued. CN-2026-0025 attached to billing record. Marking this thread resolved.

Sam (Finance): Follow-up: Engineering to add a dedupe step in prorate pipeline and make sku_tag transitions atomic. Priya or Marta, add test to renewal QA to simulate timezone edgecases.

Priya (RevOps): Will add a renewal QA case and update the playbook with a pre-invoice SKU alias check. Ticket BILL-9019 created (billing proration dedupe + timezone test).

OpsBot: Ticket BILL-9019 created and assigned to eng-billing. SLA: P2, target fix in next patch window.

Vera (Customer Success): CS confirmed refund posted and customer is unblocked. Leaving a note on account that an invoice credit was issued for proration overlap.

Sam (Finance): Great. Closing out here. We'll follow up with an RCA once BILL-9019 lands.
